item.description:
Brian Kelly, founder of The Points Guy and author of 'How to Win at Travel' joins Scarlet Fu and Tom Keene on "Bloomberg Money." They discuss how Brian Kelly initially came up with the idea to create 'The Points Guy'.

Brian Kelly, founder of The Points Guy and author of 'How to Win at Travel' joins Scarlet Fu and Tom Keene on "Bloomberg Money." They discuss the best credit card strategies for points and cash back.

item.description: Brian Kelly, founder of The Points Guy and author of 'How to Win at Travel' joins Scarlet Fu and Tom Keene on "Bloomberg Money." They discuss the best strategies for maximizing credit card points. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Trump Doubles Down on Push for Lower Rates After Strong Jobs Report
item.description: Liz Pancotti, vice president of policy, advocacy and research at progressive advocacy group Groundwork Collaborative, said that if Trump wants lower interest rates, he should stop his war in Iran and reverse his tariffs, which will bring prices down. Pancotti said that high costs are showing up even in the push to onshore manufacturing and build data centers, as materials like lumber or aluminum are subject to tariffs. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Four-Year Degrees Are Worth It, Says SUNY Purchase President
item.description: The costs of a four-year college degree continue to rise, with an average of about $60K for private and $26k for public university. As student loan defaults topped 9 million in June, parents and students are looking at every option to make college more affordable. Bloomberg's Scarlet Fu went to the campus of SUNY Purchase in New York's Westchester County to speak with the University's President Michael Steiper to see how affordability concerns are impacting campus. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: How Americans Are Handling the Cost of College
item.description: The costs of a four-year college degree continue to rise, with an average of about $60K for private and $26k for public university. As student loan defaults topped 9 million in June, parents and students are looking at every option to make college more affordable. Bloomberg's Scarlet Fu went to the campus of SUNY Purchase in New York's Westchester County to speak with students, parents and the University's President to see how they are thinking about money. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Attacking College Costs: SUNY Students, Parents
item.description: Bloomberg's Scarlet Fu went to the campus of SUNY Purchase in New York's Westchester County on move-in day to speak with students and parents about the unique strategies they are using to pay for college. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Blowout Jobs Report Jolts Markets | Open Interest 9/4/2026
item.description: Get a jump start on the US trading day with Isabelle Lee and Michael Mckee on "Bloomberg Open Interest." Stocks fall and yields jump after a blowout jobs report. White House economic adviser Chris Phelan joins us on the labor market, inflation and rates. Plus, Anthropic moves closer to a mega IPO, OpenAI unveils its latest model, Morgan Stanley cracks down on research shared on X, and Aptera’s Co-CEO joins us on why he's betting on China to build its solar EV. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Lululemon Drops to Eight-Year Low With New CEO Inheriting a Mess
item.description:
Lululemon Athletica Inc. lowered its full-year outlook for a second straight quarter, reflecting the deepening challenges incoming Chief Executive Officer Heidi O’Neill will face when she takes over the top job next week.
Sales are now projected to be in a range of $10.35 billion to $10.5 billion in the current fiscal year that ends in early 2027. That’s down from June’s annual forecast, which was itself reduced from the previous view. The company also trimmed its outlook for earnings per share after reporting its first decline in comparable sales since the pandemic when they temporarily stopped reporting the measure.
We get reaction from Poonam Goyal, Senior US Retail Analyst for Bloomberg Intelligence. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Iraq Is in Process of Seeking Oil Tankers for Hormuz Strait Runs
item.description: Iraq is in the process of trying to hire multiple tankers to transit the Strait of Hormuz as Baghdad steps up efforts to get its crude to global markets.
item.dc:creator: Khalid Al-Ansary

item.title: VW's CEO Wins Backing for Turnaround Plans
item.description:
Europe's largest carmaker Volkswagen plans to slash an additional 50,000 jobs as it struggles to compete with cheaper Chinese rivals.
Melanie Boeff explains. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Dangote Seeks to Raise $1.6 Billion in Nigeria’s Biggest IPO
item.description: Billionaire Aliko Dangote is seeking to raise $1.6 billion in what would be Nigeria’s biggest initial public offering, selling shares in the company that operates Africa’s largest oil refinery.
item.dc:creator: Nduka Orjinmo

item.title: US Sanctions Small Turkish Investment Bank Over Iran Links
item.description: The United States sanctioned Golden Global Investment Bank, a relatively small Turkish firm, as Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent continues his efforts to isolate Iran’s economy after a muted start to a new sanctions effort.
item.dc:creator: Yash Roy and Beril Akman

item.title: Bond Traders Boost Fed-Hike Odds After Jobs, Await Inflation
item.description: Bond traders reacted to a stronger-than-expected employment report on Friday by nudging up expectations for a Federal Reserve interest-rate hike this month, capping a choppy week for Treasuries as key inflation data looms.
item.dc:creator: Michael MacKenzie

item.title: S&P 500 Slumps as Strong Jobs Growth Fuels Fed-Hike Bets
item.description: US stocks fell on Friday, with the S&P 500 Index on track to finish the week virtually unchanged after the American economy added more jobs than expected in August, raising expectations that the Federal Reserve may hike interest rates soon.
item.dc:creator: Jessica Menton

item.title: Wheat Falls as Traders Weigh Outlook for Black Sea Shipments
item.description: Chicago wheat futures extended losses on Friday, on track for a weekly decline, as traders weighed the outlook for grain shipments from the Black Sea region.
item.dc:creator: Hallie Gu, Eleanor Thornber and Dayanne Sousa

item.title: Emerging Market Currencies Post Longest Winning Run Since 2007
item.description: An index for emerging-market currencies headed for a 10th successive week of gains, its longest winning streak since 2007, even as a blowout US jobs reported briefly jolted global markets on Friday.
item.dc:creator: Giovanna Bellotti Azevedo and Beatriz Amat

item.title: Gold Falls as Strong US Payrolls Power Bets on Fed Rate Hikes
item.description: Gold fell as a stronger-than-anticipated increase in US payrolls drove bets that the Federal Reserve will be forced to raise interest rates this year.
item.dc:creator: Jack Ryan, Yihui Xie and Yvonne Yue Li

item.title: Stocks Fall as Jobs Fuel Bets Fed Will Raise Rates: Markets Wrap
item.description: A stronger-than-anticipated increase in US jobs drove stocks and short-dated bonds lower, with traders boosting their bets the Federal Reserve will raise rates this month.
item.dc:creator: Rita Nazareth

item.title: Latest Oil Market News and Analysis for Sept. 4
item.description: Oil swung in thin holiday trading as renewed fighting between the US and Iran heightened supply concerns, while rare signs of progress toward ending the Russia-Ukraine war chipped away at the geopolitical risk premium.
item.dc:creator: Mia Gindis, Paul Burkhardt and Charles Gorrivan
